 Judgment

1. Revisionist namely Kartar Singh has filed present revision petition, thereby challenging order dated 12.04.2023, passed by Ld. Trial Court in Complaint Case No. 1090/2022, vide which, Ld. Trial Court had dismissed the application of revisionist u/sec. 156 (3) CrPC.

sentences.text: In my subsequent paragraphs, parties will be referred with the same nomenclature with which they were referred before Ld. Trial Court, in order to avoid confusion.
3. Trial Court record reveal that complainant had filed an application u/sec. 156(3)CrPC against accused persons, praying for registration of FIR, before Ld. Trial Court.

The allegations in the complaint are mentioned below :-
"That in the first week of December 2007, accused persons have approached the complainant to sell one land measuring 2 acres of Khasra No. 920 and 921 situated at Village Jaitpur, Badarpur, New Delhi- 110044 and informed the complainant that they are the owners of the above-mentioned land.

Believing upon the accused,
complainant agreed to purchase the said land for a consideration amount of Rs.
98,00,000/- and an agreement to sell and purchase for the abovesaid land was executed on 17.12.2007 and complainant had paid a sum of Rs. 15,00,000/- in cash.

It was further agreed between CR No. 366/2023 2 of 9 Kartar Singh Vs. Jaipali the parties that accused persons shall obtain the required permission from the concerned revenue department for execution of the sale deed in favour of the complainant.

entities.text: CR No. 366/2023 2 of 9 Kartar Singh Vs. Jaipali
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: After the execution of agreement to sell and the payment of the advance, the complainant approached the accused persons for execution of sale deeds and handing over the possession of the above-mentioned land but the accused persons on the one pretext or the other, kept on lingering the matter.
Thereafter, accused persons had asked the complainant to make further payments so that they can apply for the permission from the concerned revenue department.

Thereafter, complainant further made the payment (in the month of September 2008, February 2009, April 2009, January 2009, February 2010, December 2009 and January 2010) of totaling to the amount of Rs. 92,50,000/- and issued receipts qua the same.
In the meanwhile, complainant got to know that accused persons had sold the abovesaid land to many people and cheated the complainant after taking huge amount of money.
There are certain civil and criminal litigations pending adjudication against them.

Further, complainant came to know that accused persons are not the owners of the land in question but only the CR No. 366/2023 3 of 9 Kartar Singh Vs. Jaipali cultivator and the original owner of the land was one Sh. Akil Mohd.
Said Akil Mohd had sold the land in question to one Manoj Malik and thereby all the accused persons had cheated the complainant.

Further, when accused persons were confronted by complainant with respect to ownership of the land in question, they had threatened the complainant of dire consequences and also threatened that they will implicate the complainant in a false and frivolous case.
It is further stated that accused persons are trying to dispossess the complainant from the aforesaid property.
Upon the same, complainant made a complaint to the SHO, PS Kalindi Kunj and also to the other higher authorities but neither the action has been taken nor complaint of the complainant lodged.
Based on said claims, complainant prayed that FIR be registered against accused persons u/sec. 420/467/468/471/120B/34 IPC."

sentences.text: 4 . Ld.

Trial Court called for Action Taken Report and in ATR dated 20.01.2023, IO had stated that the owner of the aforesaid land as per the revenue department is Akil Mohd. and had further stated that alleged accused persons Mahipal and Krishan were not aware about the aforesaid agreement between the complainant and the accused persons.
Further, accused persons did not give any satisfactory reply regarding CR No. 366/2023 4 of 9 Kartar Singh Vs. Jaipali the aforesaid agreement.

entities.text: CR No. 366/2023 4 of 9 Kartar Singh Vs. Jaipali
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Alleged accused Jaipali had informed the IO that she had only taken a friendly loan from the complainant and she also did not gave any satisfactory reply with regard to the aforesaid agreement.
Further, complainant was also inquired and has stated that same facts as mentioned in his complaint.
IO further submitted that an FIR No. 397/2014 u/sec. 420/467/468/471/120B IPC has already been registered at PS Jaitpur on the complaint of Manoj Malik qua the abovesaid land.

5. Ld. Trial Court after considering the contents of application u/sec. 156(3) CrPC and the said action taken report, dismissed the application of complainant vide impugned order dated 12.04.2023.
6.

In the revision petition, complainant claimed that Ld. Trial Court did not pass proper legal order as it erred by relying on the case titled as M/s. Skipper Beverages Pvt. Ltd. Vs. State, 92 (2001) DLT 217.
7.

entities.text: M/s. Skipper Beverages Pvt. Ltd. Vs. State, 92 (2001) DLT 217
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Ld. Counsel for complainant has argued that order passed by ld.

Trial court is illegal as Ld. Trial court should have allowed the application considering the mandate of law laid down in Lalita Kumari vs. State of UP & Ors., 1 Writ Petition (Criminal) No. 68 of 2009 of Hon'ble Supreme Court decided on 12th November 2013.

entities.text: Lalita Kumari vs. State of UP & Ors., 1 Writ Petition (Criminal) No. 68 of 2009
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further submitted that all the evidence are in the possession of accused persons and complainant cannot trace them out.

As per him,
considering the allegations made in the complaint cognizable offences are made out against the accused persons and evidence can only be collected by the CR No. 366/2023 5 of 9 Kartar Singh Vs.
Jaipali police.
He claimed that Ld. Trial Court had not appreciated the legal preposition of Section 156(3) CrPC correctly.
8. Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that respondents/ accused persons have forged the documents to cheat the complainant.
Further, Ld. Trial Court did not take into consideration the action taken report, filed by IO of PS- Kalindi Kunj.
Further, Ld. Trial Court did not take into consideration that the accused persons were not the owner of the land in question and as per the revenue record, the same was owned by one Akil Mohd.
It is further averred that accused persons are habitual offenders as they are accused persons in FIR No. 397/2014, PS Jaitpur.
It is further stated that matter needs proper investigation so as to collect that documents in respect to the accused persons.
It is claimed that since the allegations were serious and conspiracy had to be unearthed, so registration of FIR should have been ordered by Ld. Trial Court.
9. Per contra, Ld. Counsel for accused persons argued that impugned order passed by Ld. Trial Court was legally correct and needs no interference.
As per the accused persons, the complaint of the complainant was motivated as there are various litigations between the parties.

Further, all the facts are within the knowledge of complainant and there is no need for investigation after Kartar Singh vs Ms Jaipali on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15020195/
3 registration of FIR.
10. Arguments heard.
Record perused.
CR No. 366/2023 6 of 9  Kartar Singh Vs. Jaipali 11.
Impugned order was passed by Ld. Trial Court on 12.04.2023.
Present revision petition was filed by complainant on 29.05.2023, which means that it was filed within limitation period.
12. The impugned order was not an interlocutory order.

That order decided the legal rights of the parties and therefore, present revision petition is maintainable before this court.
13.
The question which needs adjudication in present revision petition, is whether impugned order is perverse, illegal or arbitrary in nature ?

In order to decide said question, I have to refer to the record of Ld. Trial Court and the law governing application u/sec. 156(3) CrPC.
14.
While deciding application u/sec. 156(3) CrPC, Ld. Magistrate is given discretion which he has to exercise after proper application of mind.
Further, the Magistrate should not order registration of FIR u/sec. 156(3) CrPC, without applying his mind, in a mechanical manner.

The powers u/sec.
156(3) CrPC, have to be exercised where the allegations are quite serious or evidence is beyond the reach of complainant or custodial interrogation appears to be necessary for recovery of some articles or discovery of facts.
15.
In the case in hand, complainant has levelled allegations against accused no. 1 to 3, which were direct and specific.

The alleged agreement to sell and receipts of payment regarding cash payment of Rs. 92,50,000/- which are all undated, are also in possession of CR No. 366/2023 7 of 9 Kartar Singh Vs. Jaipali complainant.

Regarding the factum that the accused persons had forged the documents, is the averment made by the complainant only in the present revision petition and was never made in his complaint before Ld. Trial Court.

Further, it is averred by the complainant/
revisionist that after the agreement entered upon between the parties in December 2012, several payments were made to the accused persons all by way of cash and receipts were executed, however,
several receipts of payment relied upon by the complainant, are not dated or signed by the accused persons.
Further, it is admitted by the complainant in his complaint that there are several civil cases pending between the parties in respect of the land in question.

All in all, based on said allegations,
no police investigation is required as all the documents pertaining to the transactions between the complainant and accused persons, is in the possession of the complainant for which he is already having civil litigation with the accused persons.
The net result is that, complainant has personal knowledge about the chain of events and the manner and mode in which the payments were made which led to the commission of alleged offences.
No police investigation is required for unearthening any relevant fact.
In case, any police assistance is required, then facts of this case are such that said assistance can be taken by Ld. Trial Court u/sec. 202 (1) CrPC.
Thus, application u/sec. 156(3) CrPC had no merit.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Ld. Trial Court rightly dismissed the said application vide impugned order.

More so where,
complainant failed to give any reason regarding any shortcoming in the application of mind by Ld.
Magistrate, while passing impugned order.
That order is a reasoned CR No. 366/2023 8 of 9 Kartar Singh Vs. Jaipali order and is not an arbitrary order, passed in a mechanical manner.
The impugned order is neither illegal nor perverse.
It needs no interference.

Accordingly, present revision petition,
stands dismissed.
17. Copy of this judgment be sent to the Ld. Trial Court.
